questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are correct according to the passage? (I) Tonewoods are prized not only for physical properties but also for the unique acoustic resonance they provide to instruments. (II) The United States Lacey Act amendments made it compulsory for guitar companies to trace timber back to its origin with documented precision. (III) Every piece of timber within a sustainably managed forest meets the exacting standards required for premium guitar production.
questions.solution: Statement (I) restates the opening lines: tonewoods are prized 'not merely for their physical properties but for the unique acoustic resonance they impart'. Statement (II) matches the third paragraph on the Lacey Act amendments, which compel companies to trace every piece of timber back to its origin with documented precision. Statement (III) is false because the passage says only a small fraction of available timber meets the exacting standards. Hence (I) and (II) are correct. **Answer: Both (I) and (II)**
questions.passage: Directions (Q.1-10): Read the passage carefully and answer the questions given below. Behind every handcrafted guitar sold in California lies a supply chain that stretches deep into forests thousands of miles away. For decades, boutique guitar manufacturers in the state have depended on specific tonewoods - spruce for soundboards, mahogany for necks, rosewood for fingerboards - prized not merely for their physical properties but for the unique acoustic resonance they impart to an instrument. Yet the very forests that supply these materials are under mounting pressure, forcing the industry to confront an uncomfortable question: can fine guitar making survive without contributing to deforestation? The problem is not simply one of demand. Tonewoods are extraordinarily selective materials. A luthier crafting a high-end acoustic guitar requires wood that is straight-grained, free of knots, aged adequately, and harvested at precisely the right stage of the tree's maturity. This specificity means that even within a sustainably managed forest, only a small fraction of available timber meets the exacting standards that premium guitar production demands. Indiscriminate logging in pursuit of these select pieces causes disproportionate damage to surrounding forest ecosystems. Regulatory pressure has also intensified. Amendments to the United States Lacey Act have made it a federal offence to import wood harvested in violation of the laws of the source country, compelling California guitar companies to trace every piece of timber back to its origin with documented precision. Several manufacturers have responded by building direct partnerships with certified sustainable forestry operations in countries such as Canada, Germany, and responsibly managed regions of South America. Some companies have gone further, investing in alternative materials research. Composite carbon fibre necks, reclaimed urban timber, and plantation-grown alternatives such as Sitka spruce cultivated specifically for acoustic properties are gradually entering production lines. Certain manufacturers have begun seasoning and storing legally sourced wood decades in advance, building strategic timber reserves that insulate them from both supply disruptions and regulatory uncertainty. The finest guitars, it turns out, require not only skilled hands but also an ethical and carefully managed relationship with the forests that make them possible.

questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are incorrect according to the passage? (I) Composite carbon fibre necks and reclaimed urban timber are completely replacing traditional tonewoods across all guitar manufacturers. (II) Some California guitar manufacturers have built direct partnerships with certified sustainable forestry operations in Canada and Germany. (III) Certain manufacturers have begun storing legally sourced wood decades in advance to insulate themselves from supply disruptions.
questions.solution: Statement (I) is an exaggeration: the passage says alternatives like carbon fibre necks and reclaimed timber are 'gradually entering production lines', not completely replacing tonewoods across all manufacturers. Statements (II) and (III) are both clearly supported - the passage mentions partnerships with operations in Canada and Germany, and manufacturers seasoning and storing legally sourced wood decades in advance. So only (I) is incorrect. **Answer: Only (I)**

questions.q: Which of the following statements is/are TRUE about the characteristics of trees and timber required for premium guitar production? (I) Wood selected for guitar making must be straight-grained, knot-free, adequately aged, and harvested at the right stage of tree maturity. (II) Within any forest, most available trees naturally meet the strict quality standards that boutique guitar manufacturers require. (III) Selective tonewood harvesting causes damage extending beyond targeted trees to surrounding forest ecosystems.
questions.solution: Statement (I) is true - the passage describes luthier wood as straight-grained, free of knots, aged adequately, and harvested at the right stage of maturity. Statement (II) is false because only a small fraction of timber in any forest meets those standards. Statement (III) is true as indiscriminate logging for select pieces causes disproportionate damage to surrounding ecosystems. **Answer: Both (I) and (III)**

questions.q: What does the passage suggest about the role of regulatory pressure in reshaping California's guitar manufacturing industry?
options: Regulations have completely shut down guitar manufacturing by making timber imports legally impossible for boutique producers
Regulations have primarily benefited large corporations while pushing boutique guitar makers out of the market
Regulatory frameworks have encouraged guitar companies to relocate their manufacturing operations outside the United States
Federal legislation has compelled manufacturers to establish traceable and documented timber sourcing practices
questions.solution: The passage states that the amended Lacey Act made it a federal offence to import illegally harvested wood, compelling California guitar companies to trace every piece of timber back to its origin with documented precision. Options (a) to (d) all claim extreme outcomes - complete shutdown, market exit, relocation or abandonment of acoustic guitars - none of which the passage supports. Regulation is shown as forcing traceable, documented sourcing. **Answer: Federal legislation has compelled manufacturers to establish traceable and documented timber sourcing practices**
questions.shortcut: Eliminate the four extreme options; the passage only supports documented traceability.

questions.q: According to the passage, why does tonewood harvesting cause disproportionate damage even within sustainably managed forests?
options: Sustainable forest management prohibits selective harvesting making it impossible to extract only the finest quality timber
Guitar manufacturers deliberately target the oldest trees causing irreversible damage to ancient forest ecosystems
Only a small fraction of available timber meets required standards meaning much surrounding forest is disturbed during selection
Tonewood extraction requires complete forest clearing since individual tree selection is technically impossible at scale
questions.solution: The second paragraph explains that only a small fraction of available timber in even a sustainably managed forest meets the exacting standards for premium guitars, and indiscriminate logging in pursuit of those select pieces causes disproportionate damage to surrounding forest ecosystems. This is exactly what option (c) states. The other options misrepresent the passage. **Answer: Only a small fraction of available timber meets required standards meaning much surrounding forest is disturbed during selection**

questions.q: Choose the word most similar in meaning to "impart" as used in the passage.
questions.solution: In the opening line the passage says tonewoods are prized for the unique acoustic resonance they impart to an instrument, i.e., the qualities they give or convey to it. 'Convey' matches this sense, while remove, withhold, demand and extract are opposite or unrelated. **Answer: Convey**
questions.shortcut: Replace the word in context: resonance they 'give' = convey.

questions.q: Choose the word most similar in meaning to "exacting" as used in the passage.
questions.solution: 'Exacting standards' in the passage refers to standards that are very strict and demanding, which only the finest timber satisfies. 'Stringent' means exactly this. Flexible, lenient and relaxed are antonyms, and ordinary is unrelated. **Answer: Stringent**

questions.q: Choose the most appropriate word to fill in the blank: "A luthier crafting a high-end acoustic guitar requires wood that is straight-grained, free of knots, aged adequately, and ______ at precisely the right stage of the tree's maturity."
questions.solution: The sentence lists requirements of the wood used for guitar making, and the blank needs a verb done to the wood at the right stage of the tree's maturity. 'Harvested' fits perfectly - timber must be cut at the correct maturity. Planted, discarded, processed and transported do not collocate with 'stage of the tree's maturity' in this context. **Answer: harvested**

questions.q: What alternative approaches have some guitar manufacturers adopted to reduce dependence on traditional tonewoods?
options: Completely abandoning handcrafted production and shifting toward mass manufacturing using synthetic materials
Lobbying governments to relax environmental regulations to ensure continued access to traditional forest timber
Investing in composite materials, reclaimed urban timber, and plantation-grown alternatives with acoustic properties
Importing finished guitar components from countries with less stringent environmental and forestry regulations
questions.solution: The fourth paragraph directly lists the alternatives: composite carbon fibre necks, reclaimed urban timber, and plantation-grown alternatives such as Sitka spruce cultivated for acoustic properties. Option (c) summarises this exactly, while the other options describe actions the passage never mentions or contradicts. **Answer: Investing in composite materials, reclaimed urban timber, and plantation-grown alternatives with acoustic properties**

questions.q: The passage mentions that certain manufacturers have begun "seasoning and storing legally sourced wood decades in advance." What does this strategy most accurately reveal about the guitar manufacturing industry?
options: Manufacturers are stockpiling timber illegally to circumvent the provisions of the amended United States Lacey Act
Forward-looking manufacturers treat sustainably sourced timber as a long-term strategic asset rather than a routine raw material
Storing wood in advance indicates that guitar manufacturers have abandoned investment in alternative material research entirely
This practice suggests manufacturers believe plantation-grown alternatives will permanently fail to meet acoustic quality standards
questions.solution: The passage says this advance storage builds 'strategic timber reserves that insulate them from both supply disruptions and regulatory uncertainty' - showing the wood is treated as a long-term strategic asset rather than a routine input. The other options claim illegal stockpiling, abandoned research, or an intention to exit the industry, none of which the passage supports. **Answer: Forward-looking manufacturers treat sustainably sourced timber as a long-term strategic asset rather than a routine raw material**

questions.q: Rearrange the following parts (A), (B), (C) and (D) to form a grammatically and contextually correct sentence: (A) are more likely to be hospitalized (B) for heat-related illness (C) research suggests that people taking (D) antipsychotics or cardiovascular drugs
questions.solution: Starting with (C) 'research suggests that people taking', it flows into (D) 'antipsychotics or cardiovascular drugs' (object of 'taking'), then (A) 'are more likely to be hospitalized' (the verb for the people), and ends with (B) 'for heat-related illness'. The full sentence: 'Research suggests that people taking antipsychotics or cardiovascular drugs are more likely to be hospitalized for heat-related illness.' **Answer: CDAB**
questions.shortcut: Find the subject-verb chain: people taking (C-D) ... are more likely (A).

questions.q: Rearrange the following parts (A), (B), (C) and (D) to form a grammatically and contextually correct sentence: (A) manufacturers striving to (B) meet customer demand consistently (C) chain is essential for (D) designing an efficient supply
questions.solution: (D) 'designing an efficient supply' connects with (C) 'chain is essential for' to form the opening clause, which then takes the object (A) 'manufacturers striving to', completed by (B) 'meet customer demand consistently'. Sentence: 'Designing an efficient supply chain is essential for manufacturers striving to meet customer demand consistently.' **Answer: DCAB**

questions.q: Rearrange the following parts (A), (B), (C) and (D) to form a grammatically and contextually correct sentence: (A) National Statistical Office on Friday. (B) as shown by data released by the (C) a five-quarter low of 6.7 percent (D) India's GDP growth slipped to
questions.solution: (D) is the natural opener: 'India's GDP growth slipped to', which takes the figure (C) 'a five-quarter low of 6.7 percent'. The attribution follows: (B) 'as shown by data released by the' and (A) 'National Statistical Office on Friday.' Sentence: 'India's GDP growth slipped to a five-quarter low of 6.7 percent as shown by data released by the National Statistical Office on Friday.' **Answer: DCBA**

questions.q: Rearrange the following parts (A), (B), (C) and (D) to form a grammatically and contextually correct sentence: (A) cleaner, safer and more sustainable (B) challenge of decarbonizing while (C) the automotive industry faces twin (D) helping to make urban transport
questions.solution: (C) opens the sentence: 'the automotive industry faces twin', completed by (B) 'challenge of decarbonizing while'. The 'while' clause continues with (D) 'helping to make urban transport' and closes with (A) 'cleaner, safer and more sustainable'. Sentence: 'The automotive industry faces twin challenge of decarbonizing while helping to make urban transport cleaner, safer and more sustainable.' **Answer: CBDA**

questions.q: Four words in the sentence below are highlighted as options. Identify the word that is misspelt or inappropriate in usage; if all four are correct, choose 'All are correct'. Sentence: The warden considered it esential to maintain discipline among the inmates, conducting surprise inspections every alternate week.
questions.solution: 'Esential' is a misspelling of 'essential' (double 's' after 'e'). The other highlighted words - surprise, discipline and inmates - are correctly spelt and used. **Answer: esential**

questions.q: Four words in the sentence below are highlighted as options. Identify the word that is misspelt or inappropriate in usage; if all four are correct, choose 'All are correct'. Sentence: The officer promptly responded to the customer's grievance and assured him of a satisfactory resolution within two working days.
questions.solution: Officer, responded, grievance and satisfactory are all correctly spelt and contextually appropriate in this sentence about handling a complaint, so no word is erroneous. **Answer: All are correct**

questions.q: Four words in the sentence below are highlighted as options. Identify the word that is misspelt or inappropriate in usage; if all four are correct, choose 'All are correct'. Sentence: The probationer was assigned a routine task of reconciling the daily transections before the close of business hours.
questions.solution: 'Transections' is wrong - the correct spelling of the financial word is 'transactions'. Probationer, assigned and routine are all correct. **Answer: transections**

questions.q: Four words in the sentence below are highlighted as options. Identify the word that is misspelt or inappropriate in usage; if all four are correct, choose 'All are correct'. Sentence: The teller carefully counted the cash, matched it against the ledger and reported the balance to the branch manager.
questions.solution: Teller, counted, ledger and balance are all correctly spelt banking words used appropriately here, so the sentence has no erroneous word. **Answer: All are correct**

questions.q: Four words in the sentence below are highlighted as options. Identify the word that is misspelt or inappropriate in usage; if all four are correct, choose 'All are correct'. Sentence: The junoir prefect diligently supervised the morning assembly, ensuring every participant adhered to the prescribed code of conduct.
questions.solution: 'Junoir' is a misspelling of 'junior' (i-o-r vs i-o-r order - correct form is j-u-n-i-o-r). Diligently, participant and prescribed are correct. **Answer: junoir**

questions.q: A word has been given in the question and used in the sentences below. Identify the statements where the word has been used in a contextually and grammatically correct manner. WORD: BOARD. (I) The manager decided to board the proposal before presenting it to the clients. (II) The passengers were asked to board the train at Platform 4 ten minutes before departure. (III) She was invited to join the board of directors because of her extensive experience in finance.
questions.solution: In (I), 'board the proposal' is incorrect usage - one tables or presents a proposal, not boards it. In (II), 'board the train' correctly uses board as a verb meaning to get on. In (III), 'the board of directors' correctly uses board as a noun meaning a governing body. So (II) and (III) are correct. **Answer: Both (II) and (III)**
questions.shortcut: Test each sentence against the known senses of 'board' (get on / governing body).

questions.q: Which of the following words will fit in the given blank (A)?
questions.solution: The sentence says it is important to ____ suitable native species according to climate and soil - i.e., to choose or 'select' them before planting. Borrow, collect, reject and disturb do not fit the sense of picking appropriate species. **Answer: select**
questions.passage: Directions (Q.21-25): In the following passage there are blanks, each denoted by a letter and a number. For each blank, five options are given; choose the most appropriate word that fits the blank. Planting trees is one of the most effective ways to improve the environment, but achieving long-term success requires following certain steps. Before beginning any plantation drive, it is important to ____(A)____ suitable native species according to the local climate and soil conditions. Experts recommend preparing the land properly, ensuring adequate spacing, and combining tree planting with water conservation measures so that young plants receive the support they need. These practices can be ____(B)____ with regular monitoring to increase the survival rate of saplings. Another important aspect is protecting newly planted trees from grazing animals, pests, and extreme weather. Local communities, schools, and volunteers can ____(C)____ together to care for the plants during the first few years, when they are most vulnerable. Simple measures such as mulching, watering during dry periods, and replacing damaged saplings will help to ____(D)____ healthy growth and improve the overall success of the project. When these guidelines are followed consistently, tree plantation campaigns can create lasting environmental benefits. They improve air quality, reduce soil erosion, support biodiversity, and make surrounding areas more resilient to climate change. Such well-planned efforts can ____(E)____ a healthier and greener future for generations to come.

questions.q: Which of the following words will fit in the given blank (B)?
questions.solution: 'These practices can be ____ with regular monitoring' needs a word showing practices are done together with monitoring. 'Combined' fits: combined with regular monitoring to raise sapling survival. Separated, removed, exchanged and postponed contradict the context. **Answer: combined**

questions.q: Which of the following words will fit in the given blank (C)?
questions.solution: 'Local communities, schools, and volunteers can ____ together' requires a verb of joint effort that pairs with 'together' - 'work'. Compete, hesitate, divide and disappear neither collocate with 'together' nor suit the cooperative tone. **Answer: work**

questions.q: Which of the following words will fit in the given blank (D)?
questions.solution: 'Mulching, watering... will help to ____ healthy growth' needs a positive verb taking 'healthy growth' as object - 'ensure'. Prevent, ignore, reduce and interrupt would all undermine growth and contradict 'improve the overall success'. **Answer: ensure**

questions.q: Which of the following words will fit in the given blank (E)?
questions.solution: 'Such well-planned efforts can ____ a healthier and greener future' needs a verb that goes with bringing a future into being - 'create'. Damage, threaten, weaken and postpone all give a negative sense that clashes with the concluding, optimistic tone. **Answer: create**

questions.q: The sentence is divided into four segments (A), (B), (C) and (D). Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error; if the sentence is entirely correct, choose 'No error'. Sentence: The frog (A)/ is capable of (B)/ surviving in (C)/ both land and water. (D)
questions.solution: 'Surviving in both land and water' is wrong because 'land' takes the preposition 'on', not 'in' - one survives on land. The error lies in segment (C); it should read 'surviving on'. **Answer: C**

questions.q: The sentence is divided into four segments (A), (B), (C) and (D). Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error; if the sentence is entirely correct, choose 'No error'. Sentence: The committee approved (A)/ the proposal (B)/ of implement the (C)/ revised procedure immediately. (D)
questions.solution: After the preposition 'of', the verb must take the gerund form - 'of implementing', not 'of implement'. The error is in segment (C). **Answer: C**

questions.q: The sentence is divided into four segments (A), (B), (C) and (D). Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error; if the sentence is entirely correct, choose 'No error'. Sentence: The athlete had (A)/ broke the previous (B)/ championship record before (C)/ turning professional. (D)
questions.solution: With the auxiliary 'had', the past participle is required: 'had broken', not 'had broke'. So the error is in segment (B). **Answer: B**

questions.q: The sentence is divided into four segments (A), (B), (C) and (D). Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error; if the sentence is entirely correct, choose 'No error'. Sentence: The horse was (A)/ in not mood (B)/ to continue the race (C)/ after the long journey. (D)
questions.solution: 'In not mood' is an incorrect word order; the correct negative phrase is 'in no mood' - 'The horse was in no mood to continue the race'. The error is in segment (B). **Answer: B**

questions.q: The sentence is divided into four segments (A), (B), (C) and (D). Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error; if the sentence is entirely correct, choose 'No error'. Sentence: The research (A)/ findings has encouraged (B)/ several institutions to (C)/ revise their policies. (D)
questions.solution: The subject is 'findings' (plural), so the verb must be 'have encouraged', not 'has encouraged'. The error of subject-verb agreement is in segment (B). **Answer: B**
